p3: confidence lowered to medium. 'lālārāma kṛṣṇadāsa' could be one person (Lālā Rāmakṛṣṇadāsa) or two (Lālārāma and Kṛṣṇadāsa).
p1: confidence lowered to medium. 'suṃjāditya' may be a corruption of Muñjāditya.
p2: confidence set to medium for the scribe role. The role is inferred from the name standing after paṭhanārthaṃ; there is no verb such as likhitam.

date.as_written: saṃvat 18||52|| māśotamāse(!) aśvana(!) māse kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśyāṃvāra ādityām

purpose: paṭhanārtham: for the reading of Lālā Rāmakṛṣṇadāsa, kṣatriya
notes: The place string 'jaikaradāśaśadṛśraṇapuramadhye' is corrupt. It probably reads as the scribe's name (jaikaradāsa) followed by 'śāharaṇapuramadhye', i.e. Saharanpur, as the catalogue says. 'lālārāma kṛṣṇadāsa' can be read as Lālā Rāmakṛṣṇadāsa (lālā being an honorific), taken here, or as two persons, Lālārāma and Kṛṣṇadāsa. 'kṣatriyādvāra' may be a Hindi-influenced 'kṣatriya dvārā', meaning 'by', but in context it is read with paṭhanārthaṃ ('for the reading of'). The author's name 'suṃjāditya' may be a corruption of Muñjāditya. 'māśotamāse' = māsottame; 'aśvana' = Āśvina. The colophon has only one era, VS 1852, which gives c. 1795 CE (Āśvina kṛṣṇa 14, Sunday).
